current_status.summary: Stage 7 box_shrink is locally useful but remains composition-quarantined. The latest scoped interaction benchmark did not justify another runtime sandbox.

validated_mechanisms.note: Stage 7 failures can produce structured non-causal candidate evidence without mutating gameplay topology.
Later-stage candidates are overlays and do not replace validated Stage 5/6 providers.
Useful for inspecting ownership, but current evidence does not justify another Stage 7 causal arbitration change.
Legal moves can be represented as ephemeral visible action hypotheses without creating persistent topology nodes.
Plan entry, progress, exit, abort, and TTL evidence made multi-ply failure windows inspectable.
Experimental behavior remained opt-in and traceable.
DTM/tablebase evidence was used only offline for labels and diagnostics, not runtime policy.
Stage 7 remains quarantined despite local improvements.

rejected_or_insufficient_paths: scoped interaction benchmark as currently implemented

evidence_for: Some Stage 7 families were solved when existing providers were forced or arbitrated differently.
Provider-score comparability and ownership repeatedly affected post-box behavior.
Stage 7 residuals look like strategic phase-boundary cases rather than pure local move failures.
evidence_against: The first unified strategy arbitration probe was small and did not identify a better owner.
Provider-local normalization and scoped interaction benchmarks did not justify causal arbitration.
hypotheses.current_read: Still plausible at the architecture level, but not solved by the Stage 7-local arbitration variants tried so far.

evidence_for: The learnable post-box provider can own residual states but still max-plies.
Some families were unresolved by existing forced providers within diagnostic horizons.
Failures persisted after first-move visibility and ownership improvements.
evidence_against: Some failed families converted when existing providers were forced.
DTM evidence shows theoretical wins within practical horizons, so the issue is not always absent chess capacity.
hypotheses.current_read: Post-box continuation capacity remains plausible, but it is entangled with strategy ownership and sequence-policy quality.

evidence_for: The 0926 CandidateMoveFrame role found exactly one converting move with visible terms.
State-local contrast found positives separable from hard negatives by single terms or interactions in many states.
Visible-term refinement identified useful candidates around king support, box progress, cut/fence, and rook geometry.
evidence_against: Simple visible-term scorers and scoped interaction benchmark did not cleanly solve ranking.
Several high-value terms are globally ambiguous and need context rather than standalone causal use.
hypotheses.current_read: Missing or under-scoped ontology is likely part of the problem, but current visible-term refinements are not sufficient as a runtime patch.

evidence_for: Learnable capsule ownership was achieved, but closed-loop conversion still failed.
Expanded DTM-margin supervision improved top-1 only modestly and left hard-negative ranking unresolved.
Simple pairwise/ranked and scoped interaction objectives failed to beat baseline cleanly.
evidence_against: Top-k signals and state-local separability show some useful representation exists.
A broader strategy or curriculum-boundary issue could be causing the training objective to chase the wrong target.
hypotheses.current_read: The current ReCoN-visible representation/training objective is insufficient to learn the post-box continuation policy cleanly.

evidence_for: Stage 7 remains local-valid but composition-quarantined after many distinct diagnostic paths.
Box_shrink near the edge appears noisy as an owner and may be better treated as local evidence or handoff trigger.
Residuals increasingly point to strategy/plan selection rather than a standalone box_shrink actuator.
evidence_against: Box_shrink local semantics are not useless and should remain available as evidence.
A stronger strategy arbiter or sequence policy might make the existing boundary usable.
hypotheses.current_read: Stage 7 should not be promoted as an independent stage now; it may need reframing as a handoff signal inside a broader KRK strategy layer.

main_conclusion.summary: The strongest conclusion is not that Stage 7 needs another patch. The current ReCoN-visible representation and training objective are insufficient for clean post-box continuation learning, and box_shrink may be a noisy strategic boundary rather than a stable independent promoted stage.
implications: Keep Stage 7 residuals as held-out challenge cases.
Move the next experiment up one architecture level.

architecture_level_options.name: Strategy Arbiter Track
architecture_level_options.description: Train/evaluate a domain-level KRK strategy arbiter over existing provider suggestions and terminal-space features.
architecture_level_options.purpose: Learn when box_shrink should yield to fence, edge-net, king-support, drive, or mate-basin strategies.

architecture_level_options.name: Sequence Policy Track
architecture_level_options.description: Develop a stronger Plan Capsule sequence-policy learner.
architecture_level_options.purpose: Learn multi-step continuation from offline trajectories and closed-loop feedback, not one-ply ranking.

architecture_level_options.name: Curriculum Boundary Track
architecture_level_options.description: Reclassify Stage 7 as an unstable boundary and redesign box_shrink as a handoff trigger rather than a promoted independent skill.
architecture_level_options.purpose: Preserve local box evidence while avoiding a brittle stage owner.

architecture_level_options.name: Broader KRK Integration Track
architecture_level_options.description: Freeze Stage 7 as a known residual and train/evaluate a broader KRK continuation layer while preserving validated Stage 5/6.
architecture_level_options.purpose: Treat Stage 7 residuals as regression cases for broader KRK plan learning.

recommended_next_architecture_direction.recommendation: Pause Stage 7 repairs and design a general KRK strategy-arbitration / plan-selection experiment outside the Stage 7 local-repair loop.
rationale: Stage 7 has become too narrow as an implementation target but valuable as a benchmark for strategy arbitration and plan learning.
Continuing to patch Stage 7 risks overfitting the virtual lab.
A higher-level KRK strategy experiment can use Stage 7 residuals as held-out challenge cases while preserving the validated Stage 5/6 stack.
